```plato
    // The radical inverse of `index` in the given base: the base's digits of the
    // index, mirrored about the point. The van der Corput sequence, and the
    // one-dimensional building block of both Halton and Hammersley. Zero for a
    // non-positive index or a base below two.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_der_Corput_sequence
    RadicalInverse(index: Integer, base: Integer): Number
        => index <= 0 || base < 2
            ? 0.0
            : ((index % base).ToNumber + RadicalInverse(index / base, base)) / base.ToNumber;

    // The Halton point of the given index: radical inverses in two bases, which
    // must be coprime or the two coordinates correlate.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halton_sequence
    HaltonPoint2D(index: Integer, baseX: Integer, baseY: Integer): Point2D
        => Point2D(RadicalInverse(index, baseX), RadicalInverse(index, baseY));

    // The Halton point of the given index in three bases, pairwise coprime.
    HaltonPoint3D(index: Integer, baseX: Integer, baseY: Integer, baseZ: Integer): Point3D
        => Point3D(RadicalInverse(index, baseX), RadicalInverse(index, baseY),
            RadicalInverse(index, baseZ));

    // The Hammersley point of index i out of count: the index's own fraction
    // along X and its radical inverse along Y. Better distributed than Halton,
    // at the price of needing the count in advance.
    HammersleyPoint2D(index: Integer, count: Integer, base: Integer): Point2D
        => Point2D(count <= 0 ? 0.0 : index.ToNumber / count.ToNumber,
            RadicalInverse(index, base));

    // The Gray-code accumulator behind the second Sobol dimension: bit k of the
    // index, when set, exclusive-ors in the k-th direction number, and the
    // direction numbers of the primitive polynomial x + 1 are generated from the
    // leading one by v -> v xor (v >> 1).
    SobolGrayCode(index: Integer, direction: Integer, accumulated: Integer): Integer
        => index <= 0
            ? accumulated
            : SobolGrayCode(index.ShiftRight(1), direction.BitwiseXor(direction.ShiftRight(1)),
                (index % 2) == 1 ? accumulated.BitwiseXor(direction) : accumulated);

    // The 2D Sobol point of the given index: the base-2 radical inverse along X
    // and the Gray-code direction sum along Y. The accumulator is 24 bits wide —
    // the mantissa a single-precision backend carries exactly, so no two distinct
    // terms round together, and 2^23 is where its leading one starts.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobol_sequence
    SobolPoint2D(index: Integer): Point2D
        => Point2D(RadicalInverse(index, 2),
            SobolGrayCode(index, 8388608, 0).ToNumber / 16777216.0);

    // One Newton step toward the positive root of x^(dimensions + 1) = x + 1,
    // repeated `steps` times from `x`. Convergence is quadratic from anywhere
    // near one, so a couple of dozen steps is far past what the mantissa holds.
    GoldenRatioRefine(dimensions: Integer, steps: Integer, x: Number): Number
        => steps <= 0
            ? x
            : GoldenRatioRefine(dimensions, steps - 1,
                x - (x.Pow((dimensions + 1).ToNumber) - x - 1.0)
                    / ((dimensions + 1).ToNumber * x.Pow(dimensions.ToNumber) - 1.0));

    // The generalized golden ratio of the given dimension: the positive root of
    // x^(d + 1) = x + 1. One gives the golden ratio, two the plastic number
    // 1.3247..., three the R3 constant 1.2207... Computed rather than tabulated,
    // so the identity that defines it is what a reader sees.
    // Precondition: dimensions is at least one — the derivative Newton divides by
    // vanishes below that.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastic_ratio
    GeneralizedGoldenRatio(dimensions: Integer): Number
        => GoldenRatioRefine(dimensions, 24, 1.5);

    // The R2 point of the given index: an additive recurrence whose increments
    // are the reciprocal powers of the plastic number, wrapped into the unit
    // square. No bases and no tables, and a lower discrepancy in the plane than
    // Halton. `offset` shifts the whole sequence; 0.5 is the usual choice,
    // because index zero would otherwise sit on the corner.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastic_ratio
    PlasticPoint2D(index: Integer, offset: Number): Point2D {
        var p = GeneralizedGoldenRatio(2);
        var n = index.ToNumber;
        return Point2D(UnitFraction(offset + n / p), UnitFraction(offset + n / (p * p)));
    }

    // The R3 point of the given index: the same recurrence one dimension up, its
    // increments the reciprocal powers of the root of x^4 = x + 1.
    PlasticPoint3D(index: Integer, offset: Number): Point3D {
        var p = GeneralizedGoldenRatio(3);
        var n = index.ToNumber;
        return Point3D(UnitFraction(offset + n / p),
                       UnitFraction(offset + n / (p * p)),
                       UnitFraction(offset + n / (p * p * p)));
    }

    //==
    // # Carrying a unit coordinate onto a region
    //
    // Every sequence above lands in the unit square or cube; every pattern below
    // reports points in world space. These two are the only bridge, so the
    // mapping is stated once.

    // The unit-square coordinate carried onto the region: (0, 0) lands on Min and
    // (1, 1) on Max.
    FromUnitSquare(region: Bounds2D, u: Point2D): Point2D
        => Point2D(region.Min.X.Lerp(region.Max.X, u.X), region.Min.Y.Lerp(region.Max.Y, u.Y));

    // The unit-cube coordinate carried onto the region.
    FromUnitCube(region: Bounds3D, u: Point3D): Point3D
        => Point3D(region.Min.X.Lerp(region.Max.X, u.X),
                   region.Min.Y.Lerp(region.Max.Y, u.Y),
                   region.Min.Z.Lerp(region.Max.Z, u.Z));

    // The area of a planar region, or zero when it is empty (inverted).
    RegionArea(region: Bounds2D): Number
        => (region.Max.X - region.Min.X).Max(0.0) * (region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y).Max(0.0);

    //==
    // # Closed-form pattern generators
    //
    // The families whose k-th point is a function of k alone: no point depends on
    // any other, so each of these is one `MapRange` and costs the same whether a
    // caller wants one point or all of them.

    // Count Halton points over the region. The sequence is taken from index one,
    // so no point lands on the region's minimum corner.
    HaltonPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer, baseX: Integer, baseY: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => count.MapRange(i => region.FromUnitSquare(HaltonPoint2D(i + 1, baseX, baseY)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: HaltonPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => HaltonPoints2D(self.Region, self.Count, self.BaseX, self.BaseY);

    // Count Hammersley points over the region.
    HammersleyPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer, base: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => count.MapRange(i => region.FromUnitSquare(HammersleyPoint2D(i, count, base)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: HammersleyPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => HammersleyPoints2D(self.Region, self.Count, self.Base);

    // Count Sobol points over the region, starting `skipCount` terms in — the
    // usual reason being to step past index zero, which is the origin.
    SobolPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer, skipCount: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => count.MapRange(i => region.FromUnitSquare(SobolPoint2D(skipCount + i)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: SobolPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => SobolPoints2D(self.Region, self.Count, self.SkipCount);

    // Count plastic (R2) points over the region.
    PlasticPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer, offset: Number): Array<Point2D>
        => count.MapRange(i => region.FromUnitSquare(PlasticPoint2D(i, offset)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: PlasticPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => PlasticPoints2D(self.Region, self.Count, self.Offset);
```
